ios.desc:
Connect to your own VPN or proxy, block ad and tracker domains, and inspect or rewrite web traffic. MintFlow brings VPN connections, flexible routing, DNS filtering, and HTTP/HTTPS debugging together on iPhone and iPad.

Use Simple Mode to send traffic through one Direct, VPN, or proxy output, or build detailed routing rules. See where connections go, investigate DNS queries, and capture the requests and responses you need.

VPN AND PROXY

- WireGuard VPN with file and QR code import
- HTTP and SOCKS5 proxies
- Pro support for AmneziaWG, Shadowsocks, Shadowsocks 2022, VMess, AnyTLS, VLESS with REALITY and Vision, Trojan, and experimental Tailscale
- Trojan over TCP or WebSocket with TLS
- Import supported VLESS, Trojan, VMess, AnyTLS, and Shadowsocks share links by pasting a link, scanning a QR code, or choosing a QR image
- Route proxy traffic through VPN connections

BUILT-IN DNS AD BLOCKING

- Free, opt-in filtering of ad and tracker domains inside MintFlow
- Choose AdGuard DNS filter, HaGeZi Multi Normal, or OISD Small
- Bundled lists let you get started without an initial filter download
- Automatic filter-list updates and manual refresh
- Keep your preferred DNS servers; no HTTPS decryption certificate required for DNS filtering
- Check domains against a filter and inspect blocking decisions in DNS Log

FLEXIBLE ROUTING AND DNS

- Match networks, domain sets, and domain keywords
- Choose Direct, VPN, proxy, reject, or drop actions
- Device-wide DNS with Direct DNS, DoT, and DoH
- Static DNS records with Pro
- Live settings with guidance when a VPN restart is required

HTTPS CAPTURE AND WEB REWRITE

- Inspect HTTP/HTTPS requests, responses, headers, and bodies using MITM decryption
- Capture all supported traffic or select domains, IP addresses, and TCP ports
- Search capture history and preview JSON, JavaScript, CSS, HTML, images, and more
- Rewrite URLs or response bodies with jq and JavaScript
- Explore HTTP API Research, Request Simulator, and Rewrite Lab
- Export AI-friendly analysis bundles and exchange portable .mfhrb rewrite bundles

NETWORK VISIBILITY AND TOOLS

- DNS Log with a timeline, quick domain actions, and filtering by matched rule type
- Flow Capture with destination, protocol, transfer, duration, and route details
- Pro packet capture with PCAPNG export
- Ping, Traceroute, DNS Test, VPN & Proxy Test, and profile diagnostics
- Pro iPerf3 performance tests and On-Demand VPN rules
- Siri Shortcuts integration

PORTABLE PROFILES

quotes.story_title: Ask HN: What Are You Working On? (December 2025)

quotes.text:
Hi HN,

I just got MintFlow NetStack 1.1.0 approved by Apple, which introduces app-level routing capabilities. I thought this would be a good time to share the project and some of the technical background behind its development.

Over the past two years, I’ve built two iOS VPN apps based on Tailscale. I appreciate their excellent documentation and high-quality code. However, I wanted more flexibility on the client side—particularly around local routing and split tunneling. While Tailscale now offers an App Connector feature, my use case required everything to run locally, without needing a central coordinator to distribute DNS routes.

Since I’ve been working with fd.io VPP for a while and really like its architecture, I decided to try building a WireGuard-based VPN app on top of it. VPP has a WireGuard plugin modeled after FreeBSD’s implementation (though not actively maintained). My first challenge was porting the VPP core to Darwin (the underlying OS for iOS/macOS). Thanks to recent FreeBSD support via epoll-shim, it turned out to be complex but feasible—and I eventually got VPP running on macOS.

From there, I bridged Apple’s utun interface with VPP’s host stack, handling BSD socket I/O and eventually getting a working app. Version 1.0.0 shipped with basic split tunneling based on CIDR prefixes, but that felt too limited.

So last month, I added an internal stub DNS resolver using hickory-dns (Rust-based), and enabled VPP's host stack to reconstruct TCP/UDP connections …
